title: Graceful evacuation-less upgrade sentinel for private data-plane
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We need an approach to perform private (VPC) data-plane/runtime upgrades with zero customer-visible downtime without requiring full tenant evacuation. This ticket proposes an 'evacuation-less' upgrade sentinel: a deterministic, traffic-hedging, priming-first rollout with shadow KV sync and an automated rollback playbook. The goal is to allow incremental kernel/quantization/runtime changes while keeping in-flight sessions and KV cache correctness for customers on Dedicated/Private deployments.

Problem statement: Current strategies rely on tenant evacuation, large-scale cache rehydration, or full traffic cutovers which are slow, risky, and customer-disruptive. Many on-premises/private customers cannot tolerate minutes-long session interruptions or cache cold-start behavior. We need an automated, auditable upgrade path that: (1) preserves ongoing session QoS; (2) avoids mass cache invalidations; (3) detects regressions quickly and rolls back safely; and (4) integrates with Terraform/IaC hooks used by Private deployment automation.

Design overview: The Evacuation-less Sentinel is composed of four coordinated subsystems:

1) Traffic hedging controller (edge/proxy): progressive reweighting with hedged requests. New runtime instances receive a small % of identical requests (shadow+hedge) while responses are compared asynchronously. The hedging is adaptive: scheduler starts at 0.5% and ramps by health signals. Stickiness is maintained by per-session affinity keys so active sessions continue to land on the original runtime unless hedged path proves fidelity.

2) Shadow KV sync and diff snapshots: a streaming shadow-writer writes deltas to a background KV synchronizer on the new runtime nodes; snapshots and diffs are validated via checksums before the new node starts serving non-hedged traffic. This avoids full cache drains and enables quick rollback because the old runtime retains canonical state.

3) Priming probes and fidelity gating: synthetic priming probes exercise typical prefix patterns and measure metrics (first_token_latency_p95, repeated_context_p99, kv_miss_rate, generation_divergence_score). A small evaluation harness compares outputs to a golden prompt set and triggers a health gate. Only when gates pass for X consecutive windows (configurable) does the hedged weight increase.

4) IaC/terraform hooks and rollout choreography: Terraform modules expose lifecycle hooks (pre-upgrade, post-upgrade, canary-check) that run the sentinel's verification steps. A controller Lambda (or controller-job in private control plane) coordinates Terraform apply + sentinel orchestration, recording state to the customer's audit log. The plan includes idempotent IaC changes for kernel flags, model-variant toggles, and node labels used for weighted routing.

Safety & rollback policy: Automatic rollback triggers include: fidelity regression > 3% on golden prompt set, error-rate spike > 4x baseline, or first_token_latency_p95 increase > 2x. Rollback is a 3-step atomic operation: (1) immediate reweight to 0% for new nodes (hedged stop); (2) best-effort KV diff reconciliation to reconcile writes during hedging window (background); (3) decommission new nodes and annotate the runbook with telemetry. Rollback also emits a structured incident to the on-call channel and updates the Console's rollout timeline.

Implementation plan (phases):

- Phase 1 (spike & PoC, 2 wks): implement hedging proxy extension prototype + shadow-writer for KV. Validate correctness with local cluster and a small private staging tenant. (Owner: Miguel).
- Phase 2 (IaC integration, 1 wk): extend private Terraform modules with lifecycle hooks and a controller job that coordinates apply->priming->ramp. Add telemetry endpoints to report priming status. (Owner: Priya Nair).
- Phase 3 (canary & perf experiments, 2 wks): run canaries against 5 low-risk tenants, collect divergence metrics and kv-skew windows. Iterate on gating thresholds. (Owners: Runtime Team + Perf).
- Phase 4 (automation & runbook, 1 wk): codify rollback playbook, add alerts and CircuitBreaker automation (auto-reweight on thresholds). Document Confluence runbook and release checklist.

Telemetry & observability: Add new metrics: hedged_request_ratio, hedged_response_divergence, kv_delta_backlog, cache_sync_lag_seconds. Expose these on the Console rollout page. Create a pre-configured dashboard and a PagerDuty runbook for automatic on-call paging on severe regressions.

Trade-offs considered:

- Full evacuation: safe but customer-impacting; we avoid this to preserve SLAs.
- Shadow-only (no hedging): lower risk but slower fidelity signal; hedging provides faster regression detection at modest extra cost.
- Synchronous KV replication: lower data skew but higher runtime latencies; we prefer asynchronous shadow sync with deterministic reconciliation to protect p99.

Security & compliance: The shadow sync writes must obey customer KMS/HSM policies and never leak keys. Terraform hooks will require RBAC checks; we flagged security review required. Audit events will be logged to the private control plane audit store and surfaced in the Console.

Artifacts & links:

- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/PLP-evacuation-less-sentinel
- Spike PR (github): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1328
- Terraform module draft (repo): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-terraform/tree/evac-sentinel
- Console dashboard prototype: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/evac-sentinel-canary

Open questions & decisions needed:

- Thresholds for divergence detection: Defaults proposed in doc; needs Perf signoff.
- Whether to allow hedging to write to KV directly or buffer writes and ship in batches (buffering preferred initially).
- Whether to implement controller as ephemeral Lambda or include as a job in Private control plane (prefer control plane job for air-gapped customers).

Next steps: assign perf/observability pair to finalize gating thresholds, schedule a security review next week, and merge PoC spike PR to feature branch for canary testing.
